knownLimits: No sandbox provider exists: every project-code execution (runner VERIFY/REGRESSION tests, Studio dev-run/preview) is BLOCKED SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE in production by design (FD-REL-1). Runs therefore never reach SECURITY/REVIEW/REPORT in the product until a verified OS-isolation provider (with negative isolation self-tests) is built and reviewed.
LOCAL_CLAUDE IMPLEMENT still runs before VERIFY, so a run spends one edit-only builder call before it is blocked; a run-start preflight refusal was not added (scope: gate at VERIFY as specified).

Canonical tests that keep their reviewed assertions (B3A/B3C/PS-1A runner and dev-run tests) still execute repository-owned fixtures (test-written scripts and the web-node template source from core/workos/project-templates.ts) on the host through the TEST-ONLY passthrough provider injected in test code; no AI-generated or customer code is executed. The new SBX tests use a recording provider and do not run the template server.

Packaged node-mode re-exec relies on Electron's own child_process.fork hook (verified empirically in the packaged check: provenance capture and builder broker both ran); in plain Node the same helper is a normal fork.

Broker config in the control root is a working copy refreshed from the install dir before each broker run; a same-user attacker who can write userData could race it, but the same user can also write the per-user install dir.

Desktop dev-run panel shows status BLOCKED and the 409 SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE message; the BLOCKED reason itself is not rendered as a separate fact in the Studio run panel (the run card in Work shows it).

config/orchestrator-policy.json, config/trust-root-manifest.json and scripts/start-full-auto.ps1 are intentionally not staged (PACKAGED_RUNTIME_READ_EXCLUSIONS); /v1/factory (.ai/MASTER_STATE.json) is a developer-factory route and errors in the installed app as before.
